content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes, then fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends — prices often rebound higher than forecasted after dips.
- Forecasts show persistent lag in responding to recent price declines; model delays recognition of downward momentum.
- In high-volatility periods, model overreacts to short-term noise, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast horizon, particularly around day 15–20.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the true magnitude of price corrections after major spikes — underestimates the depth of drawdowns.
- Model tends to underestimate the persistence of recent trends, especially when prices are trending upward — overestimates reversal speed.
